source_text: Such outcomes reflect causal realism in law: where parental intent aligns with prevailing medical literature showing modest aggregate benefits (e.g., CDC estimates of 1 in 100 HIV risk reduction in high-prevalence settings), courts avoid overriding decisions absent acute harm. [200]
